rejected.title: Impacts of rapid urbanisation
card: Rapid urbanisation means a city grows very fast as many people move in. It can bring benefits, such as more jobs and higher incomes.
It can also bring problems. Homes may not be built fast enough, so some people live in slums: crowded areas with poor housing and few services.
Other problems include traffic, air and water pollution, and water shortages. Cities that spread outwards can also take over farmland.
A megacity is a city of over 10 million people. These large cities tend to feel the pressures most, because so many people need homes, water and transport.
rejected.remember: Fast city growth can bring jobs and incomes, but it can also strain housing, services and the environment.

a.q: Which of these is a benefit that rapid urbanisation can bring to a city?
opts: More jobs and higher incomes
Less traffic on the roads
More farmland near the city
Cleaner air and water
a.why: Many people moving to a city can mean more work and higher incomes. The other three options are the reverse of what fast growth tends to bring. Traffic and pollution usually get worse, and farmland is often lost as the city spreads.
a.clue: Think about why people move to cities in the first place.

b.q: A city in Asia has grown from 2 million to 12 million people in 30 years. Many families now live in crowded areas with poor housing. Why is this likely?
opts: Homes were not built as fast as people arrived
Most people left the city to live in the country
Farmland spread into the city centre
The city has too few people to need more homes
b.why: When people arrive faster than homes and services can be built, some end up in slums. The city has grown, not shrunk, so a lack of people is wrong. It is the growth that creates the pressure.
b.clue: Compare how fast people arrived with how fast homes could be built.
